extracted.intended_audience: administrative practitioners, UIC staff, appeals referees, legal scholars and claimants interested in unemployment insurance appeal procedure (Canada)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria governing filing, preparation, processing, hearing, and decision-making of appeals to Boards of referees under the Unemployment Insurance Commission (Canada). Includes duties of Agents, clerks, Board composition, submissions, evidence, and limits on remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pamphlet notification content and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: When a person is notified of a decision unfavourable to him he receives... a pamphlet describing the appeal procedure; the former employer receives similar notification when advised of a decision in the claimant's favour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pamphlet informs them of their right of appeal, invites internal review before filing an appeal, advises the time limits and information required on the notice of appeal, explains subsequent stages of the procedure (including the right to attend or delegate someone to appear), recommends that the claimant attend, and ends with a brief description of the Board of referees stressing the speedy and simplified procedure and that appeal costs nothing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to file appeal and extension authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals must be filed within thirty days of the date on which the claimant or the employer receives notification of the decision (sec. 94(1) of the Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If receipt date is disputed, UIC certification that the notice was mailed is deemed evidence of receipt (sec. 120(2)). UIC may, in exceptional cases, grant an extension: Agent II may grant up to 30 days (UIC Manual sec. 442.1.5); the Regional Office up to 120 days; extensions beyond that only by the Entitlement Determination Division at headquarters, which alone may refuse an extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals may be filed simply by writing a letter to the UIC office stating the grounds for the appeal (reg. 179).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UIC asks appellants to give the date when notification of the decision was received, the claimant's social insurance number, and to indicate in which official language they wish to be heard. The notice should also indicate whether the appellant wishes to avail himself of his right to be heard and, if intending a representative to appear, must give the name and address of that representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of ambiguous notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The wording of the notice of appeal may sometimes not indicate clearly that the claimant wishes to file an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a notice expresses dissatisfaction without specifying intention to appeal, UIC Agents are instructed to contact the claimant to clarify; if unable, it is presumed there will be no appeal. If correspondence after a decision produces a new decision then differing practices exist about when the 30-day period starts (initial vs. subsequent decision) and Agents may require the claimant to obtain an extension. If notice indicates lack of understanding, Agents are to telephone, ensure understanding, and write advising 30-day filing time from receipt of that letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to be heard and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal should indicate whether the appellant wishes to be heard (recognized by reg. 182(1), (2) and (4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice is never to block access to the Board of a claimant who desires to be heard, even if he initially forewent the right. If the appellant intends someone to appear (e.g., union representative), he must provide name and address. Right to be heard includes representation or an interpreter.

rubrics_metrics.name: UIC staff assistance and prohibition on influencing appellants
rubrics_metrics.description: The pamphlet urges appellants to contact the UIC staff for assistance in preparing their appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The UIC Manual forbids employees consulted in this capacity from attempting to influence appellants regarding their presentation of facts or decision to file an appeal. Agents may instead inform appellants of outside agencies specializing in assistance to claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II duties on receipt of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of the notice of appeal, the Agent II proceeds to re-examine the file and, if he decides to uphold the decision, he acknowledges receipt of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases of labour dispute or quitting, Agent II notifies the claimant or employer as appropriate. If the disputed decision made the claimant liable for repayment of unduly paid benefits, Agent II must notify the recovery section so that recovery action is suspended pending the Board (and Umpire if necessary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special procedure for labour-dispute appeals and test-case method
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals which raise the question of the existence of a labour dispute are forwarded to the Regional Office, which prepares the submission to the Board; frequent use is made of the test-case method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a group of claimants of same grade/class of a company each appeal, UIC and the union may agree to submit only one appeal considered typical; appellants are informed and may dissociate and demand separate hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to the Board — required content (narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission contains first a narrative description of the facts surrounding the claim, in the chronological order in which they were brought to the Agent's knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative normally summarizes basic information on application and Record of Employment (employer, type of employment, salary, length, reason for termination, date of claim and antedating, date of benefit period, rate of benefit), followed by near-verbatim reports of correspondence, signed statements by claimant, third-party statements containing relevant information, and the notice of appeal. Some offices summarize contents and attach photocopies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission — inclusion of labour market statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: In theory, the statistics used by the Agent in evaluating the claimant's job search should be reproduced in the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice Agents often lack access to valid statistics and do not include them. The Umpire underlined the importance of such statistics and stated an obligation on UIC to make such data available to the Board by including them; the Board has a duty to request them where they would assist determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission — handling of medical information (confidentiality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical information obtained for sickness benefit claims is considered confidential and may only be disclosed to the Board if the Medical Advisor of the UIC feels it necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For appeals regarding sickness benefit, a summary of the medical documentation prepared with comments by the Medical Advisor, stating reasons for non-disclosure if appropriate, is appended to the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent observations and variable quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agent II is authorized to conclude his narrative with such observations as he considers will help the Board to understand his decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality varies with time available and Agent's analytical ability; some observations are subjective while others present coherent legal and factual summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent should cite statutory provisions and caselaw
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agent should normally cite the specific sections of the Act and the Regulations on which his decision is based and, if appropriate, cite relevant caselaw (reported decisions of the Umpire).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constraints: limited time (average 30–45 minutes to prepare submission) and imperfect research tools (Digest lacks proper index) mean Agents often cite only 2–3 Umpire decisions; excerpts are rarely included and it is the Board's responsibility to read the caselaw referred to by the Agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission — framing issues as questions to the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agent must summarize concisely the subject of the litigation in the form of questions addressed to the Board of referees (examples given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing as legal/factual questions (e.g., availability for work, voluntary leaving without just cause) defines the parameters of the argument before the Board and the decision required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid internal abbreviations and jargon in submission
rubrics_metrics.description: In writing his submission, the Agent must refrain from using the abbreviations used by the UIC in its internal operations or form numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission is intended for readers (Board members, appellant and interested third parties) who cannot be expected to be familiar with internal jargon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and timing of submission copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequently, the appellant, his representative and other interested parties each receive a copy of the submission. Three additional copies are sent to the clerk of the Board for forwarding to the referees who will hear the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission should, in principle, be forwarded to those involved at least one week before the date fixed for the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claimant's right to correct the submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The claimant is entitled to correct a submission which he considers incorrect or incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice, claimants rarely make use of this right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines for scheduling hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC has set deadlines: in principle, 90% of the appeals should be heard within thirty days of the notice of appeal, and no hearing should take place more than 45 days after the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical data: in sample of 101 appeals, 73 heard within 30 days, 21 within 45 days, 7 after more than 45 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerk's role in organizing sessions and selection of Board
rubrics_metrics.description: When Agents II notify him of appeals, the clerk draws up a list and organizes a session when the number of appeals justifies convening the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of appeals per half-day/day varies by region; UIC HQ feel a Board should hear 12–14 appeals a day except labour-dispute appeals. The clerk selects referees by rotation in accordance with reg. 178(1); replaces unavailable referees by next on list; confirms chairman and two referees then fixes date/time. UIC Manual requires five days' notice to referees and three days' notice to appellant/representatives/interested third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quorum and reduced panel rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board is composed of three persons the chairman and one of the members may proceed with an appeal provided the appellant or his representative consents (reg. 178(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of tie vote the chairman has deciding vote (reg. 178(6)); UIC practice is to automatically grant a second hearing to any appellant dissatisfied with a two-member Board decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumed bias and disqualification of referees
rubrics_metrics.description: A referee is prevented from participating if there is a risk of bias, which is presumed under reg. 178(4) where: (•) he is or has been a representative of the claimant or employer; (•) he is or may be directly affected; (•) he has taken any part in the proceedings of the case either on behalf of an association or as a witness or otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Umpires have sometimes declined to regard certain relationships as direct affectation; if the chairman is presumed partial the other two cannot hear because reg. 178(5) requires chairman presence — the hearing must be adjourned and re-heard before another Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be present at hearings (party list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the Board is an administrative body its proceedings are not, in principle, open to the public; only the interested parties have a formal right to be heard (reg. R. 182(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested parties normally: the claimant and, in certain cases, the employer (when directly affected). Right to be heard includes the right to be heard through a representative or an agent, or, if necessary, an interpreter. Other persons affected may attend if chairman authorizes under reg. 180(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: UIC non-representation at hearing to avoid appearance of influence
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC is not normally represented at the hearing, presumably to avoid giving appellants the impression that it is attempting to influence the Board in favour of its decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originator of decision attends only at the request of the Board, mainly to explain aspects of the file rather than to defend the UIC's position. This follows maxim that justice must be done and seen to be done; reg. 180 seems drafted with this principle in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing facts at hearing — questioning protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: The first task of the Board is to establish the facts; members are obliged, if appellant present, to question him on the basis of the facts noted in the submission or subsequent correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant is represented the Board will question representative but may question appellant directly; when appellant accompanied by interpreter the Board must keep interpreter within role because interpreters can assume role of counsel and distort first-hand account. If appellant absent the Board substitutes analysis and discussion of submission among referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witnesses — summoning, presence, and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II or the chairman may, under reg. 180(5), summon any person whose presence they deem useful; the appellant may bring any persons whose testimony he wishes to present; reg. 182(1) grants right to have them questioned by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Umpires' caselaw and courts require that the appellant be present when witnesses are questioned. Testimony given in good faith enjoys protection of privilege (sec.115). Information obtained by UIC in connection with a claim is confidential and submissions include only what Commission considers necessary; Board must obtain consent to disclose confidential information beyond that given. Evidence need not be under oath, though Board may receive testimony under oath without being obliged to give it special weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary materials available to Board and limits on citation
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist legal evaluation the Board has at disposal the Act, Regulations, Umpires' decisions, Digest of Benefit Entitlement Principles, minutes of Commissioners, UIC Manual, Bulletins, internal documents, Medical Yardsticks, and labour market statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the documentation itself and use by Boards vary by district. Although UIC permits consultation of internal documents, it requests they not be cited in support of decisions and asks Boards to base reasoning strictly on the Act, Regulations and caselaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of proceedings — usual practice and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The work of the Boards, particularly examination proceedings, are not normally recorded. Although reg. 182(2) refers to the 'report of the proceedings', in practice no such report is compiled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerk often not present; only documentary evidence of hearing in claimant's file are the submission, claimant's written observations, and the Board's decision. Exceptions: labour-dispute appeals are recorded and transcribed verbatim because of complexity and usual presence of claimant, employer, Agent II/regional representative, and union representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural incidents — referrals and adjournments
rubrics_metrics.description: If claimant brings facts not taken into account or essential factual aspects cannot be conclusively established, the chairman may refer the question to the UIC for investigation and report (reg. 181). If question of insurable employment arises it must be referred to the Minister of National Revenue under sec.105 of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common occurrence is appellant inability to attend or prepare — chairman grants adjournment. After referrals or adjournments the Board composition may change due to rotation and availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decisions and limits on remedies (ultra petita and sanctions)
rubrics_metrics.description: At conclusion of examination the Board must adjourn, confirm the Agent II's decision, rescind it or amend it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board's power to amend is limited by rule of ultra petita: an appellate body may not go beyond the claims of the parties. Specifically for disqualifications (secs.40 & 41) and penalties (sec.47), the Board may not impose sanctions harsher than those imposed by the Agent. Exceptionally the Board may impose sanctions where the Agent has not if (1) knowledge of this aspect materially affects the decision regarding the question raised by the appeal and (2) the Agent could not have known of it when he made his decision.
